riverton-site.name: Riverton Site
riverton-site.summary: An archaeological site in Illinois, the type site of the Late Archaic Riverton culture (3000-1000 BCE), excavated from 1961 and added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1978.

iva-annua.name: Marsh elder
iva-annua.summary: North American annual plant (Iva annua), also called sumpweed, in the daisy family. Native Americans historically cultivated it for its edible seed.

three-sisters-agriculture.name: Three Sisters
three-sisters-agriculture.summary: A companion-planting method combining maize, beans and squash, in which each crop supports the others, developed by Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

camassia.name: Camas
camassia.summary: Plant genus of the asparagus family native to North America, also called quamash or wild hyacinth. Its pale lilac to deep purple flowers can color whole meadows.

hohokam.name: Hohokam
hohokam.summary: A culture of the North American Southwest, in south-central Arizona and Sonora, Mexico, that existed from about 300 to 1500 CE and is known for large-scale irrigation canals.

celilo-falls.name: Celilo Falls
celilo-falls.summary: Tribal fishing area and trading site on the Columbia River, on the Oregon-Washington border, with settlements for about 15,000 years. The falls and villages were submerged in 1957 by The Dalles Dam.

adena-culture.name: Adena culture
adena-culture.summary: A pre-Columbian Native American culture (500 BC – 100 AD) of the Early Woodland period, centered on Ohio, sharing burial mounds and a ceremonial complex across nearby states.

hopewell-ceremonial-earthworks.name: Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks
hopewell-ceremonial-earthworks.summary: A World Heritage Site preserving eight monumental geometric earthworks built by the Hopewell tradition in Ohio between about 1 and 400 CE, inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.

ancestral-puebloans.name: Ancestral Puebloans
ancestral-puebloans.summary: An ancient Native American culture spanning the Four Corners region of the US, living in pit houses, clan structures and cliff dwellings, linked by a network of communities across the Colorado Plateau.

barrier-canyon-style.name: Barrier Canyon Style
barrier-canyon-style.summary: A distinctive rock-art style found mostly in Utah, chiefly painted pictographs, estimated at roughly 1,500 to 4,000 years old or older.

hopewell-tradition.name: Hopewell tradition
hopewell-tradition.summary: A network of Native American cultures and trade routes, not a single society, that flourished along Eastern Woodlands rivers from 100 BCE to 500 CE, exchanging goods and ideas.

adena-mound.name: Adena Mound
adena-mound.summary: A Native American mound near Chillicothe, Ohio, the namesake site of the Adena culture, built between 100 BC and 40 AD and containing artifacts including the Adena Pipe, Ohio's state artifact.

serpent-mound.name: Great Serpent Mound
serpent-mound.summary: A 1,348-foot-long effigy mound in Ohio, the largest serpent effigy known in the world, first surveyed in 1848 and named a National Historic Landmark in 1966.

brad-lepper.name: Brad Lepper
brad-lepper.summary: American archaeologist known for work on ancient earthworks and ice age peoples in Ohio, and curator of archaeology at the Ohio History Connection.

horseshoe-canyon-utah.name: Horseshoe Canyon
horseshoe-canyon-utah.summary: A remote canyon in Utah known for Barrier Canyon Style rock art, including pictographs and petroglyphs; part of it was added to Canyonlands National Park in 1971 to protect the art.

crystal-river-archaeological-state-park.name: Crystal River Indian Mounds
crystal-river-archaeological-state-park.summary: A pre-Columbian mound complex on Florida's Gulf coast, in use from around the 2nd century AD, including a stepped pyramid, burial mounds and carved stone markers.

fort-ancient.name: Fort Ancient culture
fort-ancient.summary: A Native American archaeological culture along the Ohio River valley from about 1000 to 1750 CE, a 'sister culture' to the Mississippian culture, credited with introducing maize farming to Ohio and linked to the Great Serpent Mound.

alligator-effigy-mound.name: Alligator Effigy Mound
alligator-effigy-mound.summary: Ceremonial earthwork in Granville, Ohio, built between AD 800 and 1200 by the Fort Ancient culture, one of only two surviving effigy mounds in the state.

newark-earthworks.name: Newark Earthworks
newark-earthworks.summary: A complex of ancient earthworks in Newark and Heath, Ohio, built by the Hopewell culture between 100 BCE and 400 CE, containing the largest earthen enclosures in the world and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

newark-ohio.name: Newark, Ohio
newark-ohio.summary: A city in Licking County, Ohio, and county seat, home to much of the ancient Newark Earthworks complex built by the Hopewell culture.

temple-of-the-feathered-serpent-teotihua.name: Temple of the Feathered Serpent
temple-of-the-feathered-serpent-teotihua.summary: The third-largest pyramid at Teotihuacan in central Mexico, dated to around 150-200 CE, known for feathered-serpent carvings and more than a hundred sacrificial burials found beneath it.
temple-of-the-feathered-serpent-teotihua.source_title: Temple of the Feathered Serpent, Teotihuacan

kiva.name: Kiva
kiva.summary: An underground room used by Puebloans for spiritual ceremonies, worship and political meetings, evolved from earlier pit-houses and found among ancient ruins across the Southwestern United States.

point-peninsula-complex.name: Point Peninsula complex
point-peninsula-complex.summary: An Indigenous culture in Ontario and New York from 600 BCE to 700 CE, known for introducing thinner, better-fired pottery, likely influenced by the Hopewell tradition.

basketmaker-culture.name: Basketmaker culture
basketmaker-culture.summary: A prehistoric culture of the pre-Ancestral Puebloans in the American Southwest, lasting from about 1500 BCE to 750 CE, named for the many woven baskets found at its sites.

marksville-culture.name: Marksville culture
marksville-culture.summary: Archaeological culture of the lower Mississippi, Yazoo and Tensas valleys and the Gulf Coast, active 100 BCE to 400 CE, contemporary with the Hopewell cultures and ancestral to the Natchez and Taensa peoples.

hopewell-culture-national-historical-par.name: Mound City
hopewell-culture-national-historical-par.summary: A Hopewell culture archaeological site in Ross County, Ohio, formerly a separate National Monument and now one of four sites making up this national historical park.

hopeton-earthworks.name: Hopeton Earthworks
hopeton-earthworks.summary: An Ohio Hopewell culture site of mounds and earthwork enclosures near Chillicothe, part of the Hopewell Culture National Historic Park.

chillicothe-ohio.name: Chillicothe, Ohio
chillicothe-ohio.summary: A city in Ohio along the Scioto River, twice the state's capital and birthplace of Shawnee leader Tecumseh, near the Hopewell's Hopeton earthworks.
